tagline: A reformed thief tilts a velvet music hall by touching glowing stones, tunes a radio that rewrites the room's rules, and slides five stolen things out through brass slots without being heard.
overview:
Velvet Orchestra is a first-person physics puzzle in one dark red hall. Five stolen things stand around the room (an armchair, a table, a crate, a barrel and a potted plant) and each has to leave through one particular brass slot in the walls. You never carry them. Instead, touch one of the three glowing stones on velvet plinths (E) and the whole room leans toward that stone: everything loose slides that way.

A teal can by the radio is the dial (E to turn it). Each of its four stations rewrites one rule: Static leans gently, Waltz leans hard, Hush stops the lean and makes no noise, and Inverse pushes everything away from the stone. Every touch, every swing of your bat and every turn of the dial makes noise. Enough noise brings the Listener, a tall draped figure with one huge ear, to one of the slots, where he blocks returns and listens for you.
story: Tonight a thief returns everything they ever stole, one thing at a time, through the brass slots of an old music hall. The radio plays a waltz, the room leans toward whatever the thief last touched, and somewhere a very patient Listener is waiting to hear them. Empty the hall and there is nothing left but you.
goal: Push all five stolen things out through their slots (Returned 5/5): "Nothing left but you". If the Listener hears you three times (Heard 3/3), you lose.
rules: Each thing has its own slot: the armchair and the table leave by the WEST slot, the crate and the plant by the EAST slot, the barrel by the NORTH slot. Anything pushed into the wrong slot stays in the room.
Touch a glowing stone (E) to make it the weight: the room leans toward it. The west stone leans west, the east stone east, the north stone north.

The teal can by the radio is the dial. E turns it to the next station: 88.1 Static (gentle lean), 94.5 Waltz (strong lean), 101.2 Hush (no lean and no noise), 107.7 Inverse (everything is pushed away from the stone). The line at the top of the screen names the station.
Noise: touching a stone +3, turning the dial +4, swinging your bat +2 (none of it counts while on Hush). Noise drops by 1 every 2 seconds.
At 6 noise the Listener appears at the next slot (west, then east, then north) and stays about 12 seconds. A thing pushed into his slot bounces back to where it started.
If noise reaches 5 while he is listening, he hears you (Heard +1). Three times and the night is over.

controls.action: Touch a glowing stone, or turn the dial (the teal can)
Swing the bat to knock things by hand (noisy)

characters.name: The Thief
characters.description: Returning everything, one night at a time, with a baseball bat for nudging things.

characters.name: The Listener
characters.description: A tall draped figure with one huge ear turned to the room. He appears at a slot when you are noisy, blocks it, and counts what he hears.

characters.name: Glowing stones
characters.description: A glowing cone on a velvet plinth with a ring of light, one each on the west, east and north sides. The last one you touched is where the room leans.

characters.name: The Radio
characters.description: A walnut cabinet radio. The glowing teal can in front of it is the dial.

characters.name: Brass slots
characters.description: Brass-framed openings low in the west, east and north walls, where returned things leave the hall.

tips: Start with the west stone: two things (the armchair and the table) go out of the west slot.
Switch to Waltz for a strong lean when things are stuck, and to Hush when you need to calm the noise or nudge something by hand.
Count your noise before acting: a stone touch (3) plus a dial turn (4) is already enough to call the Listener.
If the Listener is at the slot you need, wait for him to leave (about 12 seconds) and stay quiet.

gallery.caption: The start: the dark velvet hall, the west stone glowing on its plinth.
Touching the west stone: the room now leans west.
With the room leaning west, the loose things slide toward the west wall and its brass slot.
Turning the dial (the teal can) to 94.5 Waltz: RETURNED 1/5.
The west slot has taken the armchair and the table: RETURNED 2/5.

why_made:
Idea Forge dealt this card: you tune a radio dial where every frequency rewrites one rule of the room; but gravity points toward the last thing you touched; noise draws a patient listener that always arrives from a new direction; empty the level until nothing is left but you; and, as optional story, a thief who must return everything they ever stole, one night at a time.

The AI kept the whole card: the dial has four stations that each change a rule, the room leans toward the last stone you touched, noise brings the Listener to a new slot each time, and you win when the hall is empty. It said the engine had no real gravity direction or loops over objects, so the lean is about 45 generated pushes toward three walls (not toward the stone itself) and most of its 94 rules are copies of three templates.
why_made_note: The AI did not write down its reason at the time. This is reconstructed from the idea card it was given and its own summary from the run on 2026-10-12.
